dna.default: graph=cube - `cube` is the `_` branch of connections_for and returns the twelve-pair literal that was welded into create_graph, in the same order, so the same twelve CSGCylinder3D edges are built between the same node ids. Every other constant is untouched: node_count 8, spring_length 2.0, spring_strength 0.1, repulsion_strength 50.0, damping 0.9, the 10.0 velocity clamp and the 6.0 position bound. layout_seed defaults to 0, and at 0 create_graph issues the same two global randf() calls per node in the same order, so the shipped jitter is bit-identical and two layouts in one room still start differently. warmup_steps defaults to 0, so _ready is the shipped two calls and the graph still starts tangled on its ring and untangles while you watch. time_scale defaults to 1.0, at which dt IS delta and _process is the shipped body. All 9 placements pass no config key - the richest token in the corpus is `force_directed_layout:0:0:0.6` in GT_Layout, which is rotation and y-offset, not config - so the rebuild branch in apply_grid_config is unreachable from every map that exists, and it additionally refuses to fire before the tree is built.
dna.was: no exports at all. Eight plain `var`s, twelve hard-coded connections, and an apply_grid_config whose entire body was `pass`. The runner refused it for NO TURNABLE KNOBS and it was the literal truth. WORTH RECORDING SEPARATELY: this entry's own `interactions` list still tells a reader to 'tune spring_strength and repulsion_strength in exports' and to 'change node_count to alter density'. Those exports have never existed. The claim was false when it was written and it is false now; only `graph` and the three bench knobs are settable, and that is what this block declares.
dna.note: graph is WHICH GRAPH THE SAME FORCE LAW IS ASKED TO DRAW. The description promises that 'clusters, bridges, and peripheral nodes appear as energy redistributes' - a claim about GRAPHS that a single welded adjacency could never test, because with one graph there is nothing for the layout to be a property OF. Every value keeps eight nodes and the identical springs, repulsion, damping and bounds; only the adjacency changes. cube is the shipped twelve pairs, which are the 3-cube Q3: two 4-cycles joined by four rungs, 3-regular and vertex-transitive. ring is C8, eight edges, every node the same degree and no hierarchy anywhere. star is K1,7, a tree, one hub of degree 7 against seven leaves of degree 1 - maximal hierarchy, and the only value with a node that nothing pushes out of the middle. clique is K8, all 28 edges, where there is nothing to reveal because everything is adjacent to everything, and the springs pull it into the tightest blob of the five. bipartite is K4,4, sixteen edges, every one crossing between two classes and none inside either, so the drawing contains no odd cycle at all.
dna.kin: IT IS NOT grid3d_force_directed, and the two must not be read as one family. That token was declined on 2026-08-05 in grid3d.json after considering graph = random|tree|ring|clique|lattice, and its own decline note says so: it runs commons/substrates/grid3d/grid3d_substrate.tscn through cartridge_force_directed.gd, a scene shared by nine tokens, and shares no line with this script. Its blocker does not apply here and the difference is the reason. That force law has NO bounding term, so equilibrium SIZE is set by edge count - the very thing the axis turns - and the dense values photograph as dots inside the sparse ones' frame. This one clamps every position to a 6.0 box in update_positions, and its .tscn additionally carries two fixed indicators at x = -8 and x = +8. So the extent is 12 x 12 at EVERY value (measured: all five settle against the clamp by 240 steps) and the frame is set by furniture that does not move. The union camera is identical for all five here, which is exactly what it could not be there.
dna.still_note: MEASURED by re-implementing the integrator and the harness camera in Python at the rig's real numbers, then rasterising node spheres and edge cylinders. At warmup 480 and framing 5.5: subject 4.67% of frame, peak pairwise 5.39% (clique vs bipartite), weakest pair 2.21% (ring vs star) - every pair over the 2.0% bite threshold. THE FRAMING NUMBER IS LOAD-BEARING AND FRAGILE, and here is why. This artifact is built ENTIRELY from CSG - CSGSphere3D nodes, CSGCylinder3D edges, CSGBox3D indicators - and capture_config_sweep._subtree_aabb counts MeshInstance3D and MultiMeshInstance3D only. It therefore measures NOTHING and falls back to its 1 m default box, which puts the camera 5.4 m from a 17 m object and photographs a 3.3 m window on it. framing 5.5 is calibrated against that fallback box, not against the artifact: it puts the camera at 29.6 m for a 18.1 m frame, and the furthest projected point of any of the five layouts lands at 328 px of the 380 px half-frame. IF ANY MeshInstance3D IS EVER ADDED TO THIS SCENE the fallback stops firing and this number becomes wrong by a factor of eleven. The obvious alternative - a layers=0 anchor sized to the real extent, which is what the brief recommends for this class - was measured and REJECTED: _auto_ground_artifact walks CSGShape3D too, the current min_y of about -4.2 sits just inside its 5.0 m correction cap, and an anchor spanning the true -6.3 would push it over the cap and stop three live placements being lifted at all. The fix for the bench would have been a regression in the maps. THE FIXTURE IS THE REST. warmup_steps=480 runs the shipped integrator at a fixed 1/60 delta so the still is not a fact about frame rate, time_scale=0.0 parks it there, layout_seed=1 pins the starting jitter. relax() deliberately skips update_visuals inside its loop, because every CSG property write rebuilds that shape's mesh.
dna.declines: `path` (P8) was implemented, measured and dropped. It is C8 minus one edge, and under this force law - where 50/d^2 repulsion overwhelms 0.1*(d-2) springs until every node is pressed against the 6.0 clamp - the two settle to layouts 0.31% of frame apart, against a 2.0% threshold. A duplicate tile, and the measurement is why it is not in the list. `stress` - what a node's appearance claims, size|none|heat|degree - was designed and refused on arithmetic. update_visuals scales each node by 1 + min(force * 0.1, 0.5), and at 480 steps the mean residual force is 0.7-2.4, so the scale sits at 1.07-1.24: a 20% radius change on eight small discs that are perhaps a third of a 4.67% subject, which lands near 0.5% of frame. It would ship and return a verdict about the bench. spring_strength, repulsion_strength, damping and spring_length stay plain untyped vars: they set how HARD the same drawing is pulled, and turning them is a dial on one picture. node_count is a density knob and would break the twelve-pair literal that `cube` exists to preserve.
dna.underlying_finding: Two real defects were found on the way and are deliberately NOT papered over by this promotion. The .tscn declares ForceIndicator as a CSGCylinder3D, while setup_indicator_materials fetches it through get_or_create_box_indicator and animate_indicators then guards with `if force_indicator is CSGBox3D` - so the force bar has never once resized in any placement; only the energy bar, which really is a CSGBox3D, responds. And the shipped repulsion has no equilibrium inside the frame: every graph in the family, including the shipped cube, ends pressed flat against the 6.0 clamp within four seconds, so what the room actually shows after a moment is not a force balance but a box holding eight nodes apart. Both are decisions to make, not axes to declare.

entry.name: Graph Basilica
entry.description: A walk-in basilica that IS a graph — node-piers, an edge-beam vault, floor-plan adjacency, and a BFS light-wave rolling through the structure every six seconds.
F_repel = k/r^2 (all pairs), F_spring = -k*(L-L0) (edges only). Repulsion spreads nodes apart; springs hold connected nodes together. Layout is equilibrium.
entry.name: forcedirected3d
Salesman Knot
entry.description: A 2.4 m floor plate carrying ONE closed tour of a 28x28 lattice, after Robert Bosch's 'Knot?' (2006). From across the room the dark gaps organise into a trefoil woven over and under itself; from directly above, the pale thing you are standing on resolves as a single line that visits all 784 cities exactly once and never crosses itself. Both readings are true of the same geometry and the only variable is where you stand. The tour is a boustrophedon Hamiltonian circuit — exact, not solved: row 0 runs the full width, rows 1..n-1 serpentine through columns 1..n-1, column 0 is the return spine, and it closes only on an EVEN row count, so an odd count is decremented rather than accepted. The figure is NOT made by rerouting, because it cannot be: on a Hamiltonian circuit through a uniform lattice every city has degree 2 and every edge is one grid step, so total drawn length is N*pitch however the tour runs and ink coverage is exactly stroke/pitch, constant and independent of routing. Bosch makes his picture by stippling 5000 cities where the image is dark; that needs a solver and 2-opt run to convergence, and a nearest-neighbour tour self-crosses constantly, which would cost the artifact its one claim. So the picture is made by STROKE WIDTH instead, modulated by the (2,3) torus knot x=(2+cos3t)cos2t, y=(2+cos3t)sin2t, z=sin3t, with z deciding which strand is in front at each of its three crossings and the under strand erased inside the over strand's halo — that background break IS the over-and-under. Cities may jitter off their cell centres, seeded, inside a bound that keeps the claim provable: two parallel runs one pitch apart with stroke w touch when 2a + w >= p, so a < p(1-w/p)/2 keeps every city strictly inside its own cell and two edges still meet only where they share a vertex. Measured at the shipped defaults (2026-09-09, Python mirror, seed 2006): 784 cities each visited once, every edge one grid step, closes, and 0 self-crossings brute-forced over all 307k edge pairs with jitter applied; pitch 81.4 mm, stroke 11.4 mm in the cord and 53.7 mm on the ground, never less than 13.1 mm of black between adjacent runs — measured over every non-incident edge pair with the jitter applied, where 27.7 mm is the same figure with jitter off and was what this entry claimed first — coverage 14% against 66%, albedo 0.152 against 0.608 for a ratio of 3.98:1. Reviewed 2026-09-09: the knot field was scaled as if the cord had no width, so the lobe pointing at +x overshot the outermost lattice run by 71 mm and photographed cut flat against the frame; KNOT_FILL went 0.94 to 0.84, which is where all three lobes close. The whole tour is one MultiMesh of scaled BoxMesh instances — 1568 of them, one draw call, ~18.8k triangles — rather than a hand-written ribbon, because a primitive box has correct clockwise winding, normals and tangents by construction and 19k hand-wound faces do not. The plate is a slab, never a quad, so it does not vanish edge-on; the origin is its base, so it does not stand half in the floor where auto-grounding is skipped; the collider is 16 mm tall because the stack is 16 mm tall. The corpus's first travelling salesman and first Hamiltonian circuit.

measurements.source: procedural: an 8 mm ink slab the full panel, a 16 mm metal rail round it, and the tour as 4 mm strokes on top — nothing here is taller than the frame

dev_themes: figure and ground trading places with distance
the route that cannot be seen because every route looks the same
entry.qfep_connection: GT_Pathfinding's blurb says the shortest path 'exists whether or not you find it — structure precedes discovery'. This is the case where that sentence turns over. A tour that visits every point of a lattice once lays down the same length of line however it is routed, so nothing in the picture was decided by the path: the salesman's labour is real and completely invisible in its own product. What you read as a knot is the width, and the gaps, and the distance you are standing at. Neither reading is the illusion, which is the point — a thing can be two things without one of them being the lie.
entry.note: NEW 2026-09-09. Config keys: #size:<m> panel edge, #rows:<n> / #cols:<n> cities per side (forced even), #width:<0..0.85> the WIDEST stroke as a fraction of the lattice pitch, #inner:<0..0.85> the thinnest, #mode:knot|flat, #intensity:<0..1> lattice jitter, #generation_seed:<n>, #nodes:on|off raise a bead at every city, #frame:on|off, #solid:on|off, #color1/#color2. The two stroke keys are named `width` and `inner` because those are the two numeric keys in GridInteractablesComponent.CONFIG_PARAM_NAMES that fit; a key not on that list is read as the tutorial's positional shorthand, so #stroke_max:0.66 would set yaw to 0.66 degrees and leave the stroke at its default, silently. NO dna.axes block: stroke_max is the axis that matters and it has not been swept. NOT captured or compiled in the session that wrote it — the owner had the editor open and a second Godot instance dies on the user:// lock.

entry.description: Grow a network that refuses root, trunk, and leaves. Recursive branching creates a scaffold, then lateral reconnections turn that scaffold into a mesh where any point can connect to any other. Adjusting reconnection probability moves the artifact between tree and rhizome, making hierarchy versus multiplicity a concrete topological choice. It brings Deleuze and Guattari into graph theory by questioning when a tree is the wrong model.

The artifact makes efficiency feel like subtraction.

entry.name: Grid3D — Prim's MST
entry.description: Prim's minimum spanning tree. Grows from source, always adding cheapest edge to frontier. Cyan frontier, green tree.
entry.qfep_connection: The tree grows by pure local greed — always the cheapest edge crossing the frontier — and still ends globally minimal, one of the few places where miserliness is provably virtuous. The cyan band is the real object: not the tree but the border where it is still deciding what to annex.
